summary.headline: PhysicsWallah Q1 FY27 revenue rose 24% YoY to INR1,054 crore; pre-Ind AS EBITDA improved to negative INR44 crore, with NEET calendar shift a drag.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue from operations was INR1,054 crore, up over 24% YoY, with online up 33% and offline and other up 14-16% (figures differ across the call). Pre-Ind AS EBITDA was negative INR44 crore (margin -4%), a 624 bps improvement from negative INR88 crore last year, while reported EBITDA was positive INR52 crore. Management attributed the enrollment softness to the NEET UG cycle shifting 5-7 weeks, which it said would have added 22-25% to offline growth. Management reiterated full-year FY27 guidance of 30% revenue growth and 100% EBITDA growth, and introduced first-time online/offline segment reporting.

financial_highlights.change: Improved 624 bps from negative INR88 crore in Q1 FY26
vs negative INR21 crore in Q1 FY26
vs negative INR152 crore in Q1 FY26; includes one-time non-cash charge from additional Saarthi IAS stake purchase
Includes INR2,000 crore IPO proceeds; QoQ cash up about INR600 crore

financial_highlights.metric: Online early learning and K-12 revenue

financial_highlights.change: Management says online margin to improve further in FY27

segments.name: Online
segments.commentary: Revenue up 33% YoY with bottom line improved about 600 bps; online K-12 enrollments rose from 0.55 million to 0.78 million (about 40-41%). Online is split into high-profit (JEE, NEET, CA, MBA, Commerce, Boards), path-to-profitability (GATE, UPSC, State PSCs, Foundation), and loss-making (NEET PG, Skills, Curious Junior, vernacular) buckets.

segments.name: Offline (Vidyapeeth, Pathshala)
segments.commentary: Revenue up 14% YoY with bottom line improved about 400 bps; Vidyapeeth is about 70% of offline and ARPU rose 7% in Q1. Management guides offline to near-profitability in FY27 and a steady-state margin of 13-15% for mature centers; Pathshala count fell from 84 to 70 as centers were converted to Vidyapeeth.

segments.name: K-12 / State boards / Vernacular
segments.commentary: State board enrollments and revenue roughly doubled, state boards operated rose from 7 to 14, and vernacular enrollments and revenue rose about 1.7x (70% enrollment growth per Q&A). Curious Junior enrollments rose 67% and collections 150%, but the category is still expected to reach break-even only this year.

segments.name: NEET PG and competitive exams
segments.commentary: NEET PG enrollments grew about 50% and collections about 100%; CA, CS and ACCA enrollments grew about 30%. NEET PG is described as a big bet but still loss-making.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance unchanged: 30% revenue growth and 100% EBITDA growth; management says Q1 revenue is in line with the annual operating plan.
Offline expected to reach near-profitability on a blended basis in FY27; steady-state offline margin target is 13-15%.
Online margins expected to improve within FY27 as NEET PG, vernacular and Curious Junior move toward break-even.
Center-level and offline profitability data to be disclosed only at end of FY27.
Divestment of Finzy Fintech expected within about a quarter; two non-binding term sheets signed.
New offline center decisions expected over the next two quarters; expansion to be opportunistic and limited to cohort-economics-fit geographies.
capex_capacity: Offline expansion slowed deliberately to focus on results and unit economics; no aggressive center addition planned.
Management estimated NEET timing shift cost about 1-1.5 lakh online enrollments and offline growth of 22-25% (vs 14% reported) had the cycle run on time.
Vidyapeeth seat utilization historically rose from 1.77 to 1.99, with 5-7% annual improvement; student-teacher ratio (previously in the 80s) expected to rise.
Capital allocation prioritises new online content and categories, organic and inorganic; personalised AI tutor in beta, to roll out next quarter.
School-integrated programme partner schools grew from 15 to more than 50 last year; asset-light model with admission guarantees from schools.
demand_pricing: NEET UG results on July 16 led to collections about 50% above last year post-results, per management.
Government exam notifications were weak, which reduced enrollments at subsidiary Utkarsh by about 800k in aggregate delta per the call.
Online ACPU is about INR4,000 per student, paid upfront annually; the online ARPU/ACPU mix is expected to trade off against enrollments.
Offline ARPU up 7% YoY in Q1, while management says competitors' ARPU is flat or shrinking despite intense competition.
Foundation has lower ARPU and teacher cost than NEET; management expects steady-state Foundation margin to exceed flagship categories over a longer horizon.

qa_highlights.question: Adjusted for NEET timing, what would online and offline growth have been, and is the 30% FY27 revenue guidance intact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said offline would have grown 22-25% (or 20-25% per one estimate) with on-time NEET; online lost about 1-1.5 lakh enrollments, offset by new categories. FY27 revenue (30%) and EBITDA (100%) guidance were reiterated.

qa_highlights.question: Why is enrollment growth weak even after NEET adjustment?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said NEET enrollments shifted from Q1 to Q2, and government exam notifications were weak (Utkarsh had about 800k delta). PW itself showed 8-9% enrollment growth in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Why did offline enrollments not rise with about 63 added centers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to NEET re-examination delaying student decisions by about 1.5 months (exam and results).

qa_highlights.question: How does online margin look and what drives it?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 online margin was about 27%. Management expects improvement as UPSC, GATE, Foundation and state boards mature and NEET PG, vernacular and Curious Junior reach break-even.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the INR600 crore quarter-on-quarter rise in cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the negative working capital model (students pay full-year fees upfront) drives a cash build each year from Q4 to Q1.

qa_highlights.question: How many offline Vidyapeeth centers are profitable now?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a Q1 figure and will disclose center-level profitability at end of FY27.

risks_watch: NEET UG cycle shift (5-7 weeks) pushed enrollments into Q2; management says the Q1 delta reverses, so verify Q2 offline and online enrollment catch-up against the 22-25% offline growth it cited as the on-time counterfactual.
Guidance rests on full-year delivery: FY27 30% revenue and 100% EBITDA growth are reiterated while Q1 offline growth was 14%; watch H1 year-to-date revenue and the offline near-profitability target.
Weak government exam notifications (Utkarsh about 800k enrollment delta per management) and a shift in ARPU/ACPU trade-off could weigh on enrollments; management says these are not rigid metrics.

Offline center-level and Vidyapeeth profitability withheld until end of FY27; Q1 segment EBITDA reconciliation and restated Q1 FY26 segment numbers (B2B and other revenue reclassification) need to be tracked for comparability.

Loss-making categories (NEET PG, Skills, Curious Junior, vernacular) and new initiatives (K-12, PW Books, AI tutor due next quarter) need to reach break-even; cash build (about INR600 crore QoQ) is seasonal and should not be read as operating profit; Finzy Fintech divestment expected within about a quarter.
key_quotes: So, the enrollments have shifted by 5 or 6 weeks, so we can witness that enrollment and that growth in the next quarter to come.
In terms of YTD revenue guidance, we are aligned with the 30% improvement in revenue.
Looking at it at a Q1 level wouldn't make a lot of sense and hence, we sort of avoid to share across that data, but we will be able to happy to revisit this at the end of FY27.
So, overall online margin are continue to be strong and Vikram will add on the specific numbers here.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on full-year guidance and the online business, repeatedly calling Q1 "in line" with the annual operating plan and attributing the enrollment gap to the NEET timing shift. It was evasive on quantified near-term metrics, declining to give Q1 offline center profitability, YTD enrollment numbers, and enrollment guidance, and deferring most forward-looking detail to the end of FY27.

adds.what: New offline center decisions (opportunistic, cohort-economics-fit geographies; no aggressive center addition planned)

growth.why: Management held FY27 guidance at 30% revenue growth and 100% EBITDA growth and Q1 revenue was up 24% YoY, but offline expansion has been deliberately slowed with no aggressive center additions and new center decisions deferred to the next two quarters, so capacity-backed growth is modest.
